stem: The four traditional types of Indian puppetry are string, shadow, rod and __________.
solution: Indian puppetry has four types: string, shadow, rod and glove (hand) puppets.

stem: The string-puppet (marionette) tradition 'Kathputli' belongs to __________.
solution: Kathputli is the famous string-puppet tradition of Rajasthan.

stem: The string puppets of Odisha are called __________.
solution: Kundhei are the string puppets of Odisha.

stem: The string-puppet form 'Gombeyatta' belongs to __________.
solution: Gombeyatta is the string-puppet tradition of Karnataka.

stem: The shadow-puppet tradition 'Tholu Bommalata' belongs to __________.
solution: Tholu Bommalata is the leather shadow-puppet tradition of Andhra Pradesh.

stem: The shadow-puppet form 'Ravanachhaya' belongs to __________.
solution: Ravanachhaya is the shadow-puppet tradition of Odisha.

stem: The shadow-puppet tradition 'Tholpavakoothu' belongs to __________.
solution: Tholpavakoothu is the shadow-puppet tradition of Kerala, performed in temples.

stem: The shadow puppets of Karnataka are called __________.
solution: Togalu Gombeyatta are the shadow puppets of Karnataka.

stem: The rod-puppet tradition 'Putul Nautch' belongs to __________.
solution: Putul Nautch (Putul Nach) is the rod-puppet tradition of West Bengal.

stem: The rod-puppet tradition 'Yampuri' belongs to __________.
solution: Yampuri is the wooden rod-puppet tradition of Bihar.

stem: The glove-puppet tradition 'Pavakoothu' belongs to __________.
solution: Pavakoothu is the glove-puppet tradition of Kerala.

stem: The puppet tradition 'Bommalattam' of Tamil Nadu combines rod and __________ puppets.
solution: Bommalattam of Tamil Nadu combines rod and string puppetry.

stem: Shadow puppets are made of __________ and shown against a lit screen.
solution: Shadow puppets are cut from translucent leather and shown against a back-lit screen.

stem: Traditional Indian puppet plays usually draw their stories from the __________.
solution: Puppet plays usually enact stories from the epics (Ramayana, Mahabharata) and local legends.

stem: The ancient martial art of Kerala, considered one of the oldest in the world, is __________.
solution: Kalaripayattu of Kerala is one of the oldest martial arts in the world.

stem: The stick/staff martial art 'Silambam' belongs to __________.
solution: Silambam is a staff-fighting martial art of Tamil Nadu.

stem: The martial art 'Gatka', using swords and sticks, is associated with the __________ of Punjab.
solution: Gatka is a martial art associated with the Sikhs of Punjab.

stem: The martial art 'Thang-Ta' (Huyen Langlon) belongs to __________.
solution: Thang-Ta (Huyen Langlon) is the martial art of Manipur.

stem: The martial art 'Mardani Khel' is associated with __________.
solution: Mardani Khel is a martial art of Maharashtra, associated with the Marathas.

stem: The traditional Indian wrestling practised in akharas is called __________.
solution: Kushti (Pehlwani) is traditional Indian wrestling practised in akharas.

stem: The traditional sport in which a gymnast performs feats on a vertical wooden pole or rope is __________.
solution: Mallakhamba involves gymnastic feats on a pole or hanging rope.

stem: Mallakhamba is especially associated with the state of __________.
solution: Mallakhamba is especially associated with Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

stem: The archery-based festival martial tradition 'Thoda' belongs to __________.
solution: Thoda is an archery-based martial tradition of Himachal Pradesh.

stem: The traditional wrestling 'Inbuan' belongs to __________.
solution: Inbuan is a traditional wrestling form of Mizoram.

stem: According to legend, Kalaripayattu is linked to the spread of martial arts to __________ through Bodhidharma.
solution: Legend links Kalaripayattu (via Bodhidharma) to the martial arts traditions of East Asia.

stem: The martial art 'Cheibi Gad-ga' (sword and shield) belongs to __________.
solution: Cheibi Gad-ga is a sword-and-shield martial art of Manipur.

stem: The martial-art dance 'Chhau' incorporates movements derived from __________.
solution: Chhau incorporates martial and combat-based movements in its dance.

stem: The wrestling-boxing martial art 'Musti Yuddha' is traditionally practised in __________.
solution: Musti Yuddha, an unarmed martial art, is traditionally associated with Varanasi.

stem: Kalaripayattu is practised in a training arena called a __________.
solution: Kalaripayattu is practised in a kalari (training pit/arena).

stem: The puppeteers manipulate string puppets (marionettes) using __________.
options: strings attached to the puppet's joints
solution: String puppets are controlled by strings attached to the puppet's joints from above.

stem: In glove puppetry, the puppet is worn on the __________.
solution: Glove (hand) puppets are worn on the hand and manipulated by the fingers.

stem: In rod puppetry, the puppet is supported and moved by __________.
solution: Rod puppets are supported and moved by rods, usually from below.

stem: The Kathputli puppeteers of Rajasthan traditionally belong to the __________ community.
solution: The Bhat community traditionally performs Kathputli puppetry in Rajasthan.

stem: The martial arts of India were traditionally linked with __________.
solution: Indian martial arts were linked with warrior training and physical culture.

stem: The shadow-puppet play is performed with the puppets held between a lamp and a __________.
solution: Shadow puppets are held between a lamp and a white cloth screen, casting shadows for the audience.

stem: The martial art 'Lathi' khela (stick fighting) is popular in __________.
solution: Lathi (stick) fighting is a traditional martial practice in Bengal and Punjab.

stem: The martial art of Kerala, Kalaripayattu, integrates combat with __________.
solution: Kalaripayattu integrates combat techniques with marma (pressure-point) healing and body control.

stem: The puppet form used in temple rituals in Kerala to narrate the Ramayana is __________.
solution: Tholpavakoothu is the ritual shadow-puppet form of Kerala temples, narrating the Ramayana.

stem: The largest puppets, worked with rods, in Bengal are the __________.
solution: Bengal's Putul Nach uses large rod puppets.

stem: Indian puppetry is significant as a __________ folk art that preserves storytelling traditions.
solution: Puppetry is a living folk art that preserves traditional storytelling.

stem: The martial art 'Kalaripayattu' is believed to be __________ years old, one of the oldest.
solution: Kalaripayattu is regarded as over a thousand years old, among the oldest surviving martial arts.

stem: The traditional glove-puppet play of Odisha, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala uses puppets made of __________.
solution: Glove puppets typically have cloth bodies with papier-mâché or wooden heads.

stem: Which of the following is a shadow-puppet tradition?
solution: Ravanachhaya of Odisha is a shadow-puppet tradition; the others are string/rod puppetry.

stem: Which of the following is a string-puppet tradition?
solution: Kathputli of Rajasthan is a string-puppet tradition; the others are shadow puppetry.

stem: Martial arts in India are often accompanied by __________ during performance/festivals.
solution: Indian martial arts performances are often accompanied by drums and music.

stem: The martial dance 'Paika Akhada' is associated with __________.
solution: Paika Akhada is a martial dance tradition of Odisha.

stem: Puppetry and martial traditions together form part of India's __________ heritage.
solution: Puppetry and martial arts are part of India's living performing-arts heritage.

stem: The martial art associated with the Nihang Sikhs and displayed at Hola Mohalla is __________.
solution: Gatka is displayed by the Nihang Sikhs during the Hola Mohalla festival.

stem: The primary purpose of traditional puppet theatre was to __________.
options: entertain and educate through moral/epic stories
solution: Puppet theatre entertained and educated audiences through moral and epic stories.

stem: The martial art most associated with the state of Kerala is __________.
solution: Kalaripayattu is the martial art most associated with Kerala.

stem: The traditional Indian puppetry forms are classified into four main types; puppets manipulated by strings are called:
solution: The four types are string (marionette), shadow, rod and glove puppets. String puppets are controlled by strings attached to the puppeteer's fingers/control bar.

stem: 'Kathputli', the famous string puppet tradition, is associated with:
solution: Kathputli is the well-known string-puppet (marionette) tradition of Rajasthan, depicting folk tales and legends of Rajasthani heroes, with wooden puppets in colourful attire.

stem: 'Tholu Bommalata', a shadow puppetry tradition using large leather puppets, belongs to:
solution: Tholu Bommalata is the shadow-puppet theatre of Andhra Pradesh, using large, translucent, colourful leather puppets to enact stories from the epics.

stem: 'Tholpavakoothu', a shadow puppet form performed in temples, is from:
solution: Tholpavakoothu is a temple shadow-puppetry of Kerala, traditionally performed in Bhagavati temples, dramatising the Ramayana with leather puppets against a lamp-lit screen.

stem: 'Ravanachhaya', an ancient shadow puppet form using one-piece leather puppets without joints, is from:
solution: Ravanachhaya is the shadow puppetry of Odisha, using slim, single-piece (non-jointed) deer-skin puppets that cast delicate, expressive shadows depicting the Ramayana.

stem: 'Pavakathakali', glove puppets styled after Kathakali characters, is a puppet tradition of:
solution: Pavakathakali is a glove-puppet tradition of Kerala, in which the puppets are modelled on Kathakali characters, enacting episodes from the epics with music.

stem: 'Putul Nautch' / 'Putul Nach', a rod-and-string puppet tradition, is found in:
solution: Putul Nach (Putul Nautch) is the rod-puppet tradition of West Bengal, Odisha and Assam, featuring large puppets manipulated by rods, often with the puppeteer partly visible.

stem: 'Yampuri', a wooden rod puppet tradition, is associated with:
solution: Yampuri is a traditional rod-puppet form of Bihar, distinctive for using puppets carved from a single piece of wood, without joints.

stem: 'Bommalattam' (Bommalatta), which combines rod and string puppetry, is a tradition of:
solution: Bommalattam of Tamil Nadu combines rod and string puppetry, using some of the largest and heaviest puppets in India, controlled from an overhead perch.

stem: 'Sakhi Kundhei' string puppets belong to which state?
solution: Sakhi Kundhei is the string-puppet tradition of Odisha, using wooden marionettes with many strings, accompanied by music and dance-like movement.

stem: 'Gombeyatta', a string-puppet form styled on Yakshagana characters, is from:
solution: Gombeyatta is the string-puppet theatre of Karnataka, with puppets styled after Yakshagana characters, enacting episodes from the epics with music and dialogue.

stem: Shadow puppets are traditionally made from ______ and viewed against a lit screen.
solution: Shadow puppets are typically made from treated animal hide (leather), often perforated and coloured, and their shadows are projected on a screen using a light source behind them.

stem: Martial art traditions in India are broadly linked to both combat and:
options: Performance, ritual, dance and physical culture
solution: Indian martial arts blend combat skill with performance, ritual, dance and physical/spiritual discipline, many surviving as living traditions in the performing-arts realm.

stem: 'Kalaripayattu', considered one of the oldest martial arts in the world, is from:
solution: Kalaripayattu, from Kerala, is among the oldest surviving martial arts, combining strikes, weaponry, grappling and healing (marma) techniques; it influenced Kathakali training.

stem: The training arena/school where Kalaripayattu is practised is called a:
solution: A 'kalari' is the traditional training ground/school for Kalaripayattu; the art derives its name from it ('kalari' + 'payattu' meaning practice/exercise).

stem: 'Thang-Ta' and 'Sarit Sarak', martial art traditions, are from:
solution: Thang-Ta (using the sword 'thang' and spear 'ta') and the unarmed Sarit Sarak are the martial arts of Manipur, linked to its ritual and performance traditions.

stem: 'Gatka', a martial art using the sword and stick, is associated with the:
solution: Gatka is a Sikh martial art of Punjab using weapons like the sword (kirpan) and stick (soti), often demonstrated at festivals and Gurpurabs.

stem: 'Silambam', a weapon-based martial art using bamboo staves, is from:
solution: Silambam is a stick/staff-fighting martial art of Tamil Nadu with ancient roots, using the bamboo staff (silambam) and other weapons.

stem: 'Mardani Khel', a martial art associated with the Marathas, is from:
solution: Mardani Khel is an armed martial art of Maharashtra developed by the Marathas, suited to the region's hilly terrain, using weapons like the sword and the patta.

stem: 'Thoda', a martial art combining archery with dance, is from:
solution: Thoda is a traditional martial art of Himachal Pradesh combining archery, music and dance, performed during festivals like Baisakhi.

stem: 'Cheibi Gad-ga', a martial art using a sword and shield, is from:
solution: Cheibi Gad-ga is a Manipuri martial art performed with a sword ('cheibi') wrapped in leather and a shield, blending combat with performance.

stem: 'Paika Akhada', a martial art tradition associated with the Paikas (warriors) who led an 1817 rebellion, is from:
solution: Paika Akhada is a martial-art gymnasium tradition of Odisha, linked to the Paika warriors who staged the Paika Rebellion (1817) against the British.

stem: 'Kalaripayattu' has a healing component based on knowledge of vital points called:
solution: Kalaripayattu incorporates knowledge of marma (vital points) of the body, used both in combat and in a traditional healing/massage system associated with the art.

stem: Which martial art strongly influenced the training and movements of Kathakali dancers?
solution: Kalaripayattu's rigorous physical training, footwork and body control deeply influenced Kathakali, whose performers often undergo similar conditioning.

stem: 'Inbuan', a form of wrestling, is a traditional martial sport of:
solution: Inbuan is a traditional form of wrestling from Mizoram with strict rules, requiring competitors to grip a belt and avoid certain moves.

stem: 'Kushti' (Pehlwani), traditional wrestling practised in mud pits, is trained in a:
solution: Kushti/Pehlwani, Indian traditional wrestling, is practised and trained in an 'akhara' (wrestling arena), a tradition prominent across North India.

stem: 'Musti Yuddha', a form of unarmed combat/boxing, has ancient roots and is associated with:
solution: Musti Yuddha is a traditional unarmed martial art/boxing form with ancient roots, historically associated with Varanasi and parts of North India.

stem: The puppet form that uses puppets worn on the hand like a glove is the:
solution: Glove (hand) puppets are worn on and manipulated by the puppeteer's hand and fingers; Pavakathakali of Kerala and Bengal's glove puppetry are examples.

stem: The largest and heaviest traditional puppets in India are used in:
solution: Bommalattam of Tamil Nadu uses some of the largest and heaviest puppets, combining rod and string manipulation, with puppeteers operating from an overhead platform.

stem: Shadow puppetry in India predominantly enacts stories from the:
solution: Indian shadow-puppet traditions (Tholu Bommalata, Tholpavakoothu, Ravanachhaya) predominantly dramatise episodes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

stem: 'Kathputli' puppets are typically made of:
solution: Kathputli marionettes are carved from wood, brightly painted and dressed in colourful Rajasthani cloth costumes, controlled by strings.

stem: The decline of traditional puppetry has been countered by its use in:
options: Education, social messaging and cultural revival programmes
solution: Traditional puppetry is being revived and repurposed for education, health/social-awareness campaigns and cultural tourism, helping sustain the art and its practitioners.

stem: 'Chholiya', a martial dance performed with swords and shields at weddings, is from:
solution: Chholiya is a martial sword-and-shield dance of the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, traditionally performed in wedding processions of the Rajput community.

stem: The martial art 'Kalaripayattu' is broadly divided into northern and southern styles known as:
solution: Kalaripayattu has regional styles — Vadakkan (northern) and Thekkan (southern) — differing in techniques, emphasis and lineage.

stem: 'Shastar Vidya', an ancient battlefield martial art, is associated with the:
solution: Shastar Vidya is a traditional Sikh battlefield martial art preserved by the Nihang order, focusing on weaponry and combat techniques.

stem: Puppetry and martial-art performances are often supported and documented by which national body?
solution: The Sangeet Natak Akademi supports, documents and awards performing arts including traditional puppetry and martial-art performance traditions.

stem: 'Adithada', a martial art form involving strikes and locks, is from:
solution: Adithada is a Tamil Nadu martial art incorporating kicks, punches, locks and grappling, related to the region's broader martial traditions.

stem: The distinguishing feature of Odisha's Ravanachhaya shadow puppets is that they are:
options: Uncoloured, single-piece and without joints, casting monochrome shadows
solution: Ravanachhaya puppets are made of deer skin, are non-jointed and uncoloured, producing delicate, expressive black-and-white shadows — the most stylised of Indian shadow puppetry.

stem: The traditional martial art of Kerala, Kalaripayattu, is believed by some to have influenced Asian martial arts via the monk:
solution: By tradition, Bodhidharma, a monk linked to South India, is said to have carried martial-arts knowledge to China (Shaolin), though this is legendary; it reflects Kalaripayattu's antiquity.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a puppet form with its state? (i) Kathputli – Rajasthan (ii) Tholu Bommalata – Andhra Pradesh (iii) Ravanachhaya – Odisha
solution: All three are correct: Kathputli (Rajasthan, string), Tholu Bommalata (Andhra Pradesh, shadow) and Ravanachhaya (Odisha, shadow) are traditional puppet forms of their states.
